title: How much a savings bank books at its fiscal year-end as the CECL allowance on the unguaranteed portions of its relief-era SBA 7(a) loans, when an operator's units are cross-defaulted under the same personal guarantees
subdomain: expected-credit-loss-provisioning (lifetime expected charge-offs from default and payoff hazards by months on book, conditioned on survival, with the guarantor group as the unit that defaults)
prompt_shape: one figure (the allowance to the nearest $1 million) with its split by approval fiscal year, a board note with a chart of the allowance and the unguaranteed principal, and two tables (Section 1112 payments by fiscal quarter; net charge-offs by fiscal year and approval year)

sources.origin: constructed for this task by task148/generator/build.py (seeded, deterministic) around a fictional savings bank, its SBA lending division, its borrowers and guarantors and their records, in the layouts of a lender's servicing extracts and of the reports SBA's fiscal transfer agent sends lenders; no real organisation's records, person or borrower is depicted. The prime rate path the servicing records follow is the published prime rate to December 2025, held at 6.75 per cent after.
